title: Regional backpressure amplification and protective-system tuning review
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Post-incident review of a multi-region traffic surge (2025-02-09) that caused a cascading increase in error rate and an SLO miss across two customer-facing clusters. This document summarizes the timeline, root causes, mitigations applied during the event, and concrete follow-up actions to prevent recurrence.
incident_summary: On 2025-02-09 03:12 UTC a sudden demand spike originating from a single major customer in APAC caused sustained queue growth in the apac-west serving pool. Traffic overflow policies routed a subset of requests to us-east which increased end-to-end latency; aggressive circuit breakers in eu-west then tripped when request latency to the cache degraded, causing a second-order failure mode and client-facing 5xxs. The combined event produced a 4-hour SLO miss window for p50 latency and an increased tail error-rate for affected tenants.
impact_details: SLOs impacted: p50 latency SLO (100ms target) missed for 4 hours; p99 latency degradation; overall 5xx rate increased from 0.12% baseline to 3.4% at peak. Estimated affected requests: ~1.1M requests over the 4 hour window. Two paying customers observed degraded service and opened high-priority support tickets.
timeline: 2025-02-09 03:12 UTC - First sustained microburst from customer CUST-798 across apac-west routing
2025-02-09 03:24 UTC - apac-west queue length grows > 2x normal; autoscaler scheduled additional nodes but provisioning lagged (~5 mins)
2025-02-09 03:30 UTC - Smart routing overflow begins sending 30% of new requests to us-east per routing policy
2025-02-09 03:38 UTC - KV cache misses spike in us-east due to cold prefixes leading to higher backend latency
2025-02-09 03:45 UTC - Eu-west circuit breakers configured with conservative latency thresholds begin to open for shared dependencies (cache/messaging), redirecting load and producing 502/503s
2025-02-09 04:10 UTC - On-call invoked runbook. Emergency mitigations applied: temporary per-tenant rate cap on CUST-798 and manual increase of apac-west pool via dedicated capacity override
2025-02-09 05:05 UTC - Traffic normalizes as dedicated capacity and backpressure controls take effect
2025-02-09 07:30 UTC - Incident declared resolved, continuous monitoring kept for next 48 hours
root_cause: This was a multi-factor failure: 1) A single-tenant sustained burst exceeded expected burst budget and exhausted regional headroom. 2) The smart-routing overflow policy lacks a per-origin backoff, so overflow amplified downstream cold-cache costs. 3) Circuit breaker thresholds were not adaptive to joint cache latency and node provisioning state and therefore opened too aggressively, converting latency into hard failures. 4) Autoscaler cold-start lag left transient capacity gaps; the proactive reserve for APAC was insufficient.
immediate_mitigations: Applied per-tenant emergency rate cap, manually added dedicated nodes to apac-west, temporarily relaxed circuit breaker open thresholds in eu-west, and rerouted overflow to a reserve capacity pool. These mitigations reduced error rate within ~35 minutes of application.
long_term_fixes: Implement adaptive circuit breaker that uses short-term cache-latency signals and node-provisioning status to avoid premature open states
Add per-origin exponential backoff to smart-routing overflow logic to prevent repeated redirection of cold prefixes
Create an APAC regional headroom pool (reserved short-lived capacity) that can be programmatically leased during surges
Tune autoscaler provisioning profiles: reduce cold-start median from 5m to <2m for common instance types and add fast-warm path for pre-warmed containers
Introduce synthetic SLO probes that simulate cold-cache hot prefixes across regions and alert when refill rate is slower than expected
Update load-shedding policy to support graceful degradation (token-bucket + priority classes) rather than blunt rejection once threshold is crossed
action_items: ENG-13209: Implement adaptive circuit breaker prototype and unit tests (owner: Luca Martin, due: 2025-03-14)
ENG-13210: Add per-origin backoff to smart-router and integration tests (owner: Priya Desai, due: 2025-03-07)
ENG-13211: Create APAC short-lived headroom pool and automation to lease/release capacity (owner: Mateo Alvarez, due: 2025-03-21)
ENG-13212: Autoscaler tuning: reduce provisioning cold-start (owner: Wei Chen, due: 2025-03-28)
ENG-13213: Build synthetic SLO probe dashboards + alerting (owner: Nora Patel, due: 2025-03-10)
ENG-13214: Update runbooks and on-call playbook for overflow events, include checklist for relaxing CB parameters (owner: Oncall Team, due: 2025-02-25)
ENG-13215: Roll out priority-based token-bucket load-shedding at edge with staged canary (owner: Hannah Lee, due: 2025-04-04)
tests_and_verification: Each long-term fix will have a verification plan: unit + integration tests in CI, controlled canaries in a staging ring, and a runbook-driven simulated surge test. Key success metrics: no p50 SLO miss during a 3x expected burst test, circuit breaker false-open rate <0.1% in synthetic tests, and autoscaler cold-start median <2m in staging.
postmortem_notes: Runbook gaps: the on-call checklist did not include a fast path to relax circuit breaker thresholds; adding that reduced mitigation time during the event.
Observability blind spots: dashboards showed queue growth but lacked single-pane correlation between routing overflow and cache cold misses. We'll add merged view to Console.
Customer comms: support and account teams issued initial notices within 90 minutes; we will standardize an outbound template to improve transparency for multi-region incidents.
next_steps: Approve prototype PRs for adaptive circuit breaker and smart-router backoff, begin canary rollout for APAC headroom pool, update runbooks and schedule a simulated surge test in staging during Cycle 43.
